sub.en: Look at the pairs. Which sentence is about now, and which is about every day?

items.q: The market ___ at six every morning.
items.why: Present Simple for what is normally true: every morning, usually, on Saturdays.

items.q: Look — they ___ the stalls now.
items.why: Present Continuous for what is happening at this moment: now, at the moment, look.

items.q: Edgar ___ pavement art for a living.
This week he ___ on a picture of a waterfall.
People ___ to art galleries to see his work — it’s in the street.
I ___ this city at all at the moment.
items.why: am not enjoying = right now, this period. don’t enjoy = never, in general.

tts: Good morning and welcome to the show. Today we’re talking to three very different people about their work outside in the street: Edgar Mueller, a 3D pavement artist, Laxman Rao, a tea-seller, and Harry Bakewell, a street cleaner.

So, Edgar, why do you think 3D pavement art is so popular nowadays? — The art happens outside, so people can enjoy it on their way to work. They don’t have to go to art galleries or museums to see it. They love getting close to the art and exploring it.
Laxman, you sell tea on the same corner every day. — Yes. I open at six in the morning and I close at nine at night. Right now I’m writing a play, between customers.
And Harry, what are you doing at the moment? — I’m clearing the market place. Every Saturday it’s the same: the shoppers go home and the rubbish stays.

tts: How do you find city life then, Mike? — Oh, well, I’ve only been here for a few weeks. But to be honest, I’m not enjoying it at all.
How come? — I think it’s because I’m from a small town in the country, but I just can’t get used to it. Everybody’s so rude!
How do you mean? — Well, for example, nobody’s ever on time for anything. I was at a business meeting last week and three of the six people were late.

acts.title: Saturday, ten in the morning
text: My street is dull from Monday to Friday. Nothing happens. The tower block at the end hides the sun until eleven and the only people outside are the street cleaners, who come at six and leave before anybody wakes up.

On Saturday it changes. The market place fills up by nine and by ten it is crowded. Right now, from my window, I can see a pavement artist drawing something enormous in blue chalk, two women arguing about a parking space, and a street performer setting up next to the statue. Nobody is buying anything from him yet.

The stalls sell the same things every week: vegetables, cheap phone cases and, for some reason, forty kinds of sock. I always buy my vegetables here and I always pay too much for them, and I don’t mind.
By six the shoppers have gone and the rubbish is everywhere. On Sunday the cleaners come back. Nothing happens again until Saturday.

write.q: Describe your street: 6 sentences. Three about what normally happens (Present Simple, with a frequency word), and three about what is happening right now (Present Continuous).
write.model: My street is usually quiet during the week. The cleaners come at six every morning and nobody else is outside before eight. On Saturday the market place fills up and it gets crowded by ten. Right now I can see two women arguing about a parking space. A street performer is setting up next to the statue, and nobody is watching him yet. I’m writing this instead of doing the shopping.
